questions.stem: A student is given four substances: methane (CH₄), sodium chloride (NaCl), carbon dioxide (CO₂), and ethanol (C₂H₅OH). Which substances are organic compounds?

options.text: All four, because they all contain carbon
Methane and ethanol only, because they contain carbon bonded to hydrogen in chains or rings
Only sodium chloride, because it comes from natural sources
Carbon dioxide and methane only

questions.explanation: Organic compounds contain carbon atoms bonded to hydrogen (and often other elements like oxygen) in chains or rings. Methane (CH₄) and ethanol (C₂H₅OH) fit this definition. Carbon dioxide (CO₂) contains carbon but is classified as inorganic, and NaCl contains no carbon at all. Not all carbon-containing compounds are organic.

questions.stem: Propane has the molecular formula C₃H₈ and butane has the formula C₄H₁₀. They are consecutive members of the same homologous series. What is the molecular formula of pentane, the next member?

options.text: C₅H₁₀
C₅H₁₂
C₅H₁₄
C₆H₁₂

questions.explanation: Each successive member of the alkane homologous series differs by CH₂. From C₄H₁₀ (butane), adding CH₂ gives C₅H₁₂ (pentane). Alternatively, alkanes follow the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂, so for n=5: H = 2(5)+2 = 12, giving C₅H₁₂.

questions.stem: A chemist discovers two compounds with the same molecular formula C₂H₆O but different structural arrangements and properties. What are these compounds called?

options.text: Isotopes
Isomers
Homologues
Allotropes

questions.explanation: Isomers are compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements. C₂H₆O can be ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH, an alcohol) or dimethyl ether (CH₃OCH₃, an ether). They have very different properties — ethanol is a liquid that dissolves in water, while dimethyl ether is a gas. Isotopes are atoms with different neutrons, and allotropes are different forms of the same element.

questions.stem: In a displayed formula, a carbon atom is shown with four lines extending from it. What do these lines represent, and why are there always four?

options.text: They represent ionic bonds; carbon always forms 4 ions
They represent covalent bonds; carbon has 4 outer electrons and needs to form 4 bonds to achieve a full outer shell
They represent metallic bonds; carbon is a metal
They represent hydrogen bonds; carbon always bonds to 4 hydrogens

questions.explanation: Carbon has 4 electrons in its outer shell and needs 8 for a full outer shell. It therefore forms 4 covalent bonds by sharing electrons with other atoms. In displayed formulae, each line represents one shared pair of electrons (one covalent bond). This ability to form 4 bonds is why carbon can create such a huge variety of organic compounds.

questions.stem: Members of the same homologous series have the same general formula and functional group. What does this mean for their chemical reactions?

options.text: Each member reacts completely differently from all others
They all react at exactly the same rate
They undergo similar chemical reactions because the functional group determines reactivity
Only the first member of the series can undergo chemical reactions

questions.explanation: The functional group is the part of the molecule responsible for its characteristic chemical reactions. All members of a homologous series share the same functional group, so they undergo similar reactions. For example, all alcohols contain the -OH group and can undergo combustion and oxidation. However, physical properties (like boiling point) change gradually as chain length increases.
